meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'He's got such potential. I used to really look up to him'?
meta.ogDescription: Not Jordan. The line is invented dialogue from a Nov 2023 satire article on Dunning-Kruger-Times.com; Snopes rated the claim Labeled Satire.

answer.label: Not Michael Jordan — invented by a satire site
answer.authorName: Dunning-Kruger-Times.com, an ‘America’s Last Line of Defense’ satire site
answer.authorDates: Published 11 November 2023 · network owned by Christopher Blair
answer.sourceLine: Michael Jordan never said this. Snopes ↗ traced the sentence to a satirical article posted on Dunning-Kruger-Times.com on 11 November 2023 — a site whose own About Us page declares “Everything on this website is fiction” — and rated the claim Labeled Satire on 13 November 2023. The words are dialogue written for a fictional phone call, not a quotation from Jordan.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: “Michael Jordan Says He’d Like to ‘Slap Some Sense’ Into Colin Kaepernick”
Fabricated satire — Snopes, 13 November 2023, rated “Labeled Satire”

source.excerpt: “He’s got such potential,” Jordan said during a very emotional phone call with ALLOD’ Tara Newhole, “I used to really look up to him.”
trail: Snopes ↗, in a fact-check published 13 November 2023 by Taija PerryCook, rated the claim Labeled Satire and traced it to an article posted on Dunning-Kruger-Times.com on 11 November 2023, reproducing the line in full.

Dunning-Kruger-Times describes itself on its own About Us page ↗ as “a subsidiary of the ‘America’s Last Line of Defense’ network of parody, satire, and tomfoolery,” and states plainly: “Everything on this website is fiction.”

Jordan’s only documented comment on anthem protests points the other way. In a statement to the Charlotte Observer reported by CNN ↗ on 25 September 2017, he said those who peacefully express themselves “should not be demonized or ostracized.”

The sentence appears nowhere among the sourced quotations on Wikiquote’s Michael Jordan page ↗, which carries no misattributed or disputed section at all; a search of Quote Investigator returns no entry for it either.
source.excerptNote: As transcribed by Snopes ↗ from the originating satirical article. The phone call and the interviewer are part of the invention — the publisher’s own About Us page states that “Everything on this website is fiction.” What circulates online is the two sentences with the framing stripped away, which is precisely what makes them read as a real quotation.

author.name: Michael Jordan
author.heading: About Michael Jordan
author.metaLine: Born 17 February 1963 · Six-time NBA champion and former owner of the Charlotte Hornets
author.bio: Michael Jordan won six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls across three stints between 1984 and 2003, and later owned the Charlotte Hornets. He is a magnet for invented political quotations precisely because he says so little in that register — CNN observed in 2017 that Jordan had “famously refused to take stances on anything political” until he condemned police killings of African-Americans in July 2016. When he finally did address anthem protests, in September 2017, he defended the players’ right to kneel — the opposite of what this fabricated line has him saying.

misattribution.heading: A fake built for the share button
misattribution.intro: This is not a garbled version of something real. It is dialogue invented for a satirical news story, stripped of its framing and passed around as though Jordan had actually said it.

items.why: Snopes ↗ rated the claim Labeled Satire and reproduced the line from the originating article; Jordan is not on record saying it anywhere.

items.scope: The wider story — that Jordan wanted to ‘slap some sense’ into Colin Kaepernick
items.why: Jordan publicly backed athletes who knelt, telling the Charlotte Observer in a statement reported by CNN ↗ on 25 September 2017 that those who peacefully express themselves “should not be demonized or ostracized.”

items.scope: The interview it supposedly came from
items.why: The interviewer and the “very emotional phone call” exist only inside the satirical article; the publisher’s About Us page ↗ states that “Everything on this website is fiction.”

misattribution.truthLine: The only people who ever said these words are satirists writing in Michael Jordan’s voice, in a story Snopes rated ‘Labeled Satire’ ↗ two days after it appeared.

context.heading: Fake quotes fill silences
lead: Fabricated quotations work best where there is a vacuum, and Michael Jordan spent decades making one. CNN ↗ noted in 2017 that he had “famously refused to take stances on anything political” until July 2016, so an invented Jordan opinion on kneeling NFL players reads, to someone scrolling past, like the scoop it is pretending to be.

The tell is inside the sentence itself. Jordan was born in 1963 and his NBA career ended in 2003; Colin Kaepernick was born in 1987 and played in the NFL from 2011 to 2016. “I used to really look up to him” is not a line the older, long-retired, far more famous man plausibly delivers about the younger one — it was written for effect, and it is the half of the story that survives once the satire label falls off.
context.detailsSummary: More on the network that made it
detailsBody: Dunning-Kruger-Times.com is one of the sites in the “America’s Last Line of Defense” network, whose About Us page ↗ is signed “~Christopher Blair, AKA Busta Troll” and describes the network’s mission as showing its credulous readership “the light, through shame if necessary.” The disclaimer is public and unambiguous; it simply does not travel with the screenshot.

Snopes ↗ recorded that the Facebook post carrying the story had drawn 836 likes and 278 comments at the time of writing — a modest number that still illustrates the pattern: the article is shared, the quotation is lifted out of it, and the quotation outlives every link back to the source that would have flagged it as fiction.
context.pull: Everything on this website is fiction.

sourcesVerified.claim: Snopes, in a fact-check by Taija PerryCook published Nov. 13, 2023, rated the claim 'Labeled Satire' and traced it to an article published Nov. 11, 2023 on Dunning-Kruger-Times.com, a subsidiary of the 'America's Last Line of Defense' network. The page literally reproduces: "He's got such potential," Jordan said during a very emotional phone call with ALLOD' Tara Newhole, "I used to really look up to him." It also quotes the site disclaimer 'Everything on this website is fiction' and records the Facebook post as having 836 likes and 278 comments.

Dunning-Kruger-Times.com's own About Us page describes the site as 'a subsidiary of the "America's Last Line of Defense" network of parody, satire, and tomfoolery', states 'Everything on this website is fiction', describes the mission as showing readers 'the light, through shame if necessary', is signed '~Christopher Blair, AKA Busta Troll', and carries a copyright notice in Blair's name.

CNN (Katishi Maake, 25 September 2017) reports Michael Jordan's statement to the Charlotte Observer: 'One of the fundamental rights this country is founded on was freedom of speech, and we have a long tradition of nonviolent, peaceful protest. Those who exercise the right to peacefully express themselves should not be demonized or ostracized.' The article also states Jordan 'has famously refused to take stances on anything political until condemning killings of African-Americans at the hands of law enforcement in July of 2016.'
Wikiquote's Michael Jordan page does not contain the line 'He's got such potential. I used to really look up to him' among its quotations, and the page has no Misattributed or Disputed section.
Wikipedia gives Michael Jordan's date of birth as February 17, 1963, and records fifteen NBA seasons (1984-1993, 1995-1998, 2001-2003), primarily with the Chicago Bulls, with six championships.

Wikipedia gives Colin Kaepernick's date of birth as November 3, 1987, an NFL career spanning 2011 to 2016, and states he sat and kneeled during the U.S. national anthem throughout the 2016 pre-season and regular season.
Quote Investigator's site search returns no results for this quote or for Michael Jordan, so QI has no article on this line and offers no competing origin or earlier attestation.
